newsitem.title: UK: Tanker rates show premium for new ships to Asia.
newsitem.headline: Tanker rates show premium for new ships to Asia.

text.p: Rates for crude tankers on voyages from the Middle East Gulf to Asia showed a distinct premium for modern vessels on Tuesday, brokers said.
"The rate's very specific according to which ship you are talking about," said one. "It's a difference of Worldscale low 60s for a modern vessel East and the mid-50s for older tonnage."

He pointed to the 1990-built Sabang, fixed at W62 for 265,000 tonnes from the Gulf to Taiwan for Chinese Petroleum Corp, as a typical rate for a new vessel, while the 1975-built Ocean Jewel achieved only W54.5 for 260,000 tonnes for a voyage to Asia.
In the Mediterranean, 80,000 tonnes was fixed at W107.5 for the Seafalcon II from Ras Lanuf to Trieste for Veba, with the trend seen slightly downwards.
"It's softening a touch. People with early ships are fighting to get a reduction of a point or two," said one broker, who saw W105 as likely for the next fixture.
Few Cont/U.S. fixtures were seen apart from the Nord-Jahre Target which was booked for 125,000 tonnes at W98.5 from Mongstad to Halifax for Exxon.
On inter-UKC trips, 80,000 tonnes was seen around W107.5, while 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were fixed at around W175, down five points from Monday, brokers said.
In the West Africa sector, the 1976-built Corcovado was understood to have been fixed at W82.5 for 130,000 tonnes to USAC for Coastal, which brokers said was about average.
"But for modern ships you might get a bit more," one added.
In Caribs/U.S. Gulf W157.5-160 was seen typical for 70,000 tonnes, up around five points on a lack of ships and weather delays, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
